answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each identity to bonded collateral and penalizing correlated equivocation across a detected cohort: for k coordinated identities, aggregate slashing grows as O(k²), reflecting pairwise collusion evidence. Asymmetric capital depreciation compounds the impact, so controlling a larger swarm triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss upon detection, not merely k independent fines. A beacon, zephyr, or ivory identity gains no exemption.
